title: Automated Protein Normalization and Tryptic Digestion on a Biomek-NX Liquid Handler System
author: Yan Chen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b3gtqjwn
materials: After measuring protein concentration by the DC (Detergent Compatible) protein assay (Bio-Rad), export protein concentration report through MD Spectramax 250 software that controls the microplate reader. Copy the content in the exported text file and paste it into Excel, and then save as a UTF-8 format text file. Example protein concentration file.txt

Open Biomek software program from Biomek NX-S8 control computer. In the "Instrument" drop-down menu, select "Home all Axes" to prepare the instrument for use and purge air from the tubing and syringes. Biomek software that controls the operation of Biomek NX-S8 liquid handler system Homing all axes Purging air

Chemicals to prepare: Prepare 100 millimolar (mM), Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP) solution by dissolving 28.7 mg, TCEP in 1 mL, 100mM Ammonium Bicarbonate Prepare 200 millimolar (mM), Iodoacetamide (IAA) solution by dissolving 36.8 mg, Iodoacetamide in 1 mL, 100mM Ammonium Bicarbonate Prepare 1 mg/mL, Trypsin by adding 1 mL, 1mM HCl to 1 mg, Trypsin then vortex to mix Store TCEP, IAA, and Trypsin in -20C. IAA is light sensitive. Store in amber tube (Fisher Scientific, Cat.#05-402-31).

Add the following reagents to the normalized protein plate, in this order: 2.5 µL, 100 mM TCEP 2.5 µL, 200 mM IAA 1 µL, 1 mg/mL Trypsin The final concentrations will be 1 µg/µl protein (in 50 µl total volume), 5 milimolar (mM) TCEP, 10 milimolar (mM) IAA , and 1 µl Trypsin (1 mg/ml) (1:50 trypsin:protein ratio). Adjust as needed for your data acquisition protocols.

steps.title: Prepare CSV files
steps.instruction: Use MS Excel or a Jupyter notebook to normalize each protein sample to 50 µg and export two files formatted for the Biomek NX‑S8: NX‑AMBIC.csv and NX‑protein.csv.

steps.title: Load Normalization Method
steps.instruction: In the Biomek software, open “Open Method”, navigate to the Proteomics folder, and select the method “Proteomics‑Normalization Method”. Modify the method file as needed for your specific deck orientation and system components (see the attached ‘Before start’ file).

steps.title: Setup Deck for Normalization
steps.instruction: Click “Instrument Setup” → Deck Setup and arrange the deck as follows: Position 1 – Labware Reagent; Position 2 – Destination Plate: 96‑well PCR plate (non‑skirted, Thermo Fisher Cat.#AB0600) on a yellow PCR rack; Position 3 – AMBIC Reservoir (Biomek Reservoir, discontinued) containing ammonium bicarbonate buffer; Position 4 – 200 µL pipette tips (Molecular Bioproducts BioRobotix, Cat.#919‑262).

steps.title: Load Normalization CSV
steps.instruction: Click “Transfer From File” and copy the NX‑AMBIC.csv file into the method’s designated directory (e.g., C:\Users\jbei\Desktop\Proteomics Methods\CSV files\).

steps.title: Verify Normalization Volumes
steps.instruction: Click the second “View Datasets” button and confirm that the volumes are correctly displayed in 96‑well format.

steps.title: Run Normalization
steps.instruction: Click “Finish” to ensure no error messages, then click the green “Run” arrow to start the normalization protocol.

steps.title: Load Plate‑to‑Plate Method
steps.instruction: Open “Open Method”, go to the Proteomics folder, and select the method “Proteomics‑Plate to Plate Transfer”.

steps.title: Setup Deck for Transfer
steps.instruction: Click “Instrument Setup” → Deck Setup and use the same deck layout as described for the normalization step.

steps.title: Load Transfer CSV
steps.instruction: Click “Transfer From File” and copy the NX‑protein.csv file into the method’s directory (e.g., C:\Users\jbei\Desktop\Proteomics Methods\CSV files\).

steps.title: Verify Transfer Volumes
steps.instruction: Click “View Datasets” and ensure the protein transfer volumes are correctly displayed in 96‑well format.

steps.title: Manual Mix Samples
steps.instruction: Immediately before starting, use a multichannel pipette to thoroughly mix each protein sample in the destination plate.

steps.title: Run Plate Transfer
steps.instruction: Click “Finish” to confirm no errors, then click the green “Run” arrow to execute the plate‑to‑plate transfer.

steps.title: Incubate Digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at 37 °C for a period ranging from 04:00:00 to 16:00:00 (4 to 16 hours).

steps.title: Spin Digested Samples
steps.instruction: After incubation, centrifuge the plate at 14 000 rpm at ambient temperature for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Collect Supernatant and Store
steps.instruction: Pipette the supernatant into a new PCR plate, seal the plate, and store at –20 °C until ready for LC‑MS/MS analysis (e.g., Discovery Proteomics or Targeted Proteomics protocols).
